editorial:
Imagine jumping on a bus in New York City with nothing but a suitcase and a dream to reach Los Angeles, all while a scary gangster is hunting you down. That is exactly the mess Letty Morris finds herself in. She is a chorus girl just trying to get away from Legs Caffey, but the trip gets way more interesting when she meets Paul Porter. Paul is an escaped convict who ends up becoming her unlikely protector. The whole vibe of the movie feels like a classic road trip adventure where you never know if the characters will find love or a jail cell first.

You will probably love the chemistry between the two leads and the way the tension builds as the police and the gangsters close in. The pacing is snappy, though some of the dialogue feels a bit old-fashioned since it is from the thirties. If you enjoy old-school crime stories with a touch of romance, you should definitely check this out. You can find it by renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you like owning your movies in the best quality possible.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Paul and Letty are finally cornered. After a lot of running and close calls, Paul manages to take down the gangster Legs Caffey, proving he is not the bad guy the police think he is. He clears his name and settles his legal troubles, allowing him and Letty to stop running. They end up together, finding safety and love after their wild journey across the country.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old Hollywood road trip movies and romantic crime stories.
